title: One captured step
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$ be one of its work tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $C$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$ whose state is present. One step of the capture machine from the capture configuration associated with $C$ equals the capture configuration associated with the result of one step of $M$ from $C$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols
replaced:
For every live configuration of the base machine, one step of the capture
wrapper from its first-phase embedding equals the embedding of one step of the
base machine: the input head and the original work tapes move in lockstep, any
emission --- including one on the base machine's halting transition --- is
appended to the captured table rather than the real output, and the later
fresh lanes stay untouched; administrative states remain live.
